children: disclosed in an SEC filing that Vietnamese subsidiary VFVN agreed to acquire 100% of Ngoc Hoi Real Estate Investment Joint Stock Company. The total purchase price was VND30.857T, or about $1.2B. The sellers include VinFast founder Pham Nhat Vuong, who holds a majority stake, plus two minority shareholders. The deal is seen as another effort by Pham to support VinFast's

Ngoc Hoi is a real estate developer with a 20% economic interest in the consortium behind Hanoi’s International Sports Urban Area Project, a major mixed-use urban development. Vinhomes, which is an affiliate of VinFast
through Vingroup, is the consortium’s lead investor and will coordinate the project. VinFast

expects the investment will provide earnings and cash flow from property development, strengthening its finances and making more efficient use of capital. However, the company emphasized that electric vehicles and smart mobility will remain its core business.
also sees the real estate project as an opportunity to incorporate its electric vehicle and green mobility ecosystem into a large smart city development from the early planning stage.
The acquisition is expected to close in the third quarter, subject to customary conditions. VinFast
expects to finance it using existing financial arrangements with Vingroup and Mr. Pham, along with part of a planned capital injection.
